newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans up on private ending stocks forecast.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans up on private ending stocks forecast.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures were higher at midsession on a private forecast showing tight old- and new-crop ending stocks, traders said.
"If it weren't for the Sparks numbers, we'd be lower," said one floor trader.
The widely-watched Sparks Cos. of Memphis, Tenn., was said to put 1996/97 (Aug/Sept) soybean ending stocks at 115 million and 1997/98 ending stocks at 123 million bushels.
The new-crop ending stocks figure of 123 million is far below USDA's latest new crop soybean forecast of 240 million bushels and seen as supportive, traders said.
The forecasts confirmed worries about tight supplies of old-crop soybeans and spurred fresh concerns about the tightness of new-crop supplies, traders said.
Many see volatile trade this summer when Brazil and Argentina run out of soybeans for export and U.S. old crop supplies are almost depleted.
In earlier trade, local traders were buyers in July. Refco sold two million and L.B. Stern sold one million July.
At 1122 CDT, July soybeans were eight cents higher at $8.46-1/2 per bushel and other months were up 5-3/4 to eight cents.
